title: Standardize icon-edge loading behaviors and theme-aware disabled states for button variants
creator: Anika Mehta
description:
Goal: Reduce regressions and visual inconsistencies across button variants by: 1) standardizing loading animations and disabled appearances for icon-only and compound buttons; 2) adjusting edge padding for icon buttons to avoid hitbox drift across themes; 3) ensuring theme-aware color tokens are used so disabled and loading states meet contrast/a11y requirements in both light and dark themes.

Background: Recent regressions surfaced in customer reports and internal QA where icon-only buttons in dark mode exhibited jitter when toggling loading, and disabled states used hard-coded colors that fail contrast checks at small sizes. The design system currently has a mix of token-driven and hard-coded styles; recent token migrations left a few components using legacy variables.

Scope: Design deliverables, token proposals, motion specs (micro-interaction timing), and QA acceptance criteria. Engineering will implement CSS/JS changes and update the component stories. This ticket does not include reworking button variants themselves (size, spacing system), only the loading/disabled/motion/edge-padding behaviors.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Loading state shows a consistent spinner size/placement across: primary, secondary, destructive, and icon-only; spinner overlays must not shift label or icon layout.
- Icon-only hitbox and visual padding standardized: exported tokens button.iconEdgePadding and button.iconVisualPadding with values for compact/regular/large.
- Disabled state colors reference ds.button.disabled.* tokens and meet AA contrast against current background tokens for both light/dark.
- Motion spec: spinner fade-in/out duration 160ms, opacity easing cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.2,1), spinner scale 0.9->1.0 when appearing.
- All updated components pass component-level accessibility checklist and storybook visual regression tests.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Use a token-first approach: introduce new tokens rather than patching instances; this keeps migration predictable but requires a short coordinated rollout with engineering to avoid partial updates.
- Spinner overlay rather than inline spinner (keeps label positioning consistent), except for icon-only buttons where spinner replaces icon but retains visual alignment.
- Motion duration chosen to be short to feel responsive but long enough to avoid flicker; we add a 120ms minimum loading debounce in docs to avoid showing spinner for extremely short operations (engineering to implement optionally).

Artifacts and links: 
- Figma spec (final): https://figma.com/file/RwInf/button-loading-disabled-specs
- Token proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DS/Button+Loading+Tokens
- Implementation PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/4092
- Storybook preview (WIP): https://internal.redwood.com/storybook/button-loading-a11y

Implementation notes for engineers: 
- Replace legacy color usages with ds.button.disabled.text and ds.button.disabled.bg for each variant.
- Add tokens: button.iconEdgePadding.{compact,regular,large} and button.iconVisualPadding.{compact,regular,large}; update IconButton component to calculate hitbox using edge token and visual centering using visual token.
- Spinner placement: absolute overlay centered over content for labeled buttons; for icon-only, spinner uses same center and occupies same visual footprint as the icon to avoid layout shift.
- Provide feature flag (ds-loading-refactor) to rollback if any regressions are found during rollout.

QA checklist: 
- Visual regression across primary, secondary, destructive, neutral tokens in light/dark and high-contrast mode.
- Keyboard focus states preserved for both icon-only and labeled buttons when loading and disabled.
- Screen reader announcements: when button switches to loading, ensure aria-busy or aria-live guidance is present per platform guidance; coordinate with accessibility engineering.
- Snapshot tests for Storybook stories covering: default, loading short, loading long, disabled, icon-only, with label+icon, and compact sizes.

Rollout plan: 
1) Design review sign-off (this ticket) -> 2) Engineering implementation behind feature flag -> 3) Internal QA across components and internal apps (2 weeks) -> 4) Gradual release to canary customers and check console dashboards for errors -> 5) Full release and remove feature flag after one week of stability.

Follow-ups: 
- Audit other components that render inline spinners (menus, form controls) to ensure consistent token usage (separate ticket).
- Consider a small design token migration guide for frontend teams to avoid future partial migrations.
